title: Constant module sheaf morphisms are locally algebraic
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B$ a commutative ring, and $M,N$ be $B$-modules with $M$ finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\varphi:\underline M\to\underline N$ be a morphism of constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] of $\underline B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every object $U$ there is a covering sieve $S$ of $U$ such that, for each arrow $V\to U$ belonging to $S$ with $V$ not covered by the empty sieve, there is a $B$-linear map $f_V:M\to N$ inducing $\varphi|_V$ under the canonical constant-sheaf restriction comparisons on the slice $\mathcal C/V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No points or final object of $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

source.place: Tag 093S, lemma-morphism-locally-constant (3), applied on each slice; WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/ConstantSheafOver.lean, exists_mem_forall_exists_constantSheafOverHom_comp_map_eq, declaration lines 142–156 (7d675a26 sorry-map span 136–156).

proof.text: Work in a universe containing the site, $B,M,N$, so the size convention of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] applies (enlarge the site universe by a universe lift if necessary). Write $\eta^E_W:E\to\underline E(W)$ for the constant-presheaf unit for $E=B,M,N$. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying sets of the constant ring sheaf and of the constant abelian sheaves have the local representatives and local equality stated in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. On a slice $\mathcal C/V$, coverings of $W\to V$ are precisely coverings of $W$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The restricted unit is a natural transformation from the slice constant presheaf into the restricted ambient sheaf. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], it factors uniquely through a sheaf map from the slice constant sheaf, giving the canonical comparison and its compatibility with $\eta$. It is bijective on sections: any restricted section has local constant representatives upstairs, hence on the slice; their overlap equality is locally equality in the constant presheaf, so the converse gluing clause gives a section of the slice constant sheaf with that image. If two slice sections have the same image, represent them on a common refinement and use local equality upstairs to make the representatives equal, then separatedness on the slice makes the sections equal. For addition, represent both summands on a common covering using [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement]; the comparison preserves their sum there because it preserves the additive units, and separatedness gives equality before restriction. For scalar multiplication, represent the ring section and module section on a common covering; there they are $\eta^B(b)$ and $\eta^E(e)$, whose product is $\eta^E(be)$ on both sides. Preservation of units and separatedness again give equality. The ring multiplication comparison is checked by the same explicit calculation with $E=B$. These are exactly the canonical constant-sheaf restriction comparisons used in the statement.

proof.text: Fix $U$. By [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ for $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to each section $s_i=\varphi_U(\eta^M_U(m_i))\in\underline N(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement], their finitely many coverings admit a common covering $(W_a\to U)_a$ on which $s_i|_{W_a}=\eta^N_{W_a}(n_{a,i})$ for all $i$. If $r=0$ use the identity covering. Let $S$ be its generated sieve, which is covering in the topology generated by the site coverings. For every $g:V\to U$ in $S$, choose a factorization through some $W_a$; naturality of $\eta$ and $\varphi$ supplies elements $n_i\in N$ with $\varphi_V(\eta^M_V(m_i))=\eta^N_V(n_i)$.

source.place: Tags 00WK and 00W6; finite generating set as in sites-modules.tex Tag 093S(3), whose proof is omitted

proof.text: For $V$ not covered by the empty sieve, $\eta^N_V:N\to\underline N(V)$ is injective. Indeed equal images of $x,y$ give by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] a covering family on which their constant-presheaf restrictions agree. That family cannot be empty, for then the empty sieve would cover $V$. At any member its restriction maps are identities, so $x=y$. This argument applies also to any other constant abelian sheaf.

source.place: Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), local-equality clause; constant presheaf restriction maps are identities

proof.text: For this $V$, define $f_V(m)$ by writing $m=\sum_i b_i m_i$ and putting $f_V(m)=\sum_i b_i n_i$. If $\sum_i b_i m_i=0$, the $\underline B(V)$-linearity of $\varphi_V$ implies $\eta^N_V(\sum_i b_i n_i)=\varphi_V(\eta^M_V(\sum_i b_i m_i))=0$, since the constant-sheaf units preserve addition and scalar multiplication. Injectivity from Step 3 forces $\sum_i b_i n_i=0$. Hence the value is independent of the chosen expression, and adding expressions and multiplying their coefficients shows that $f_V$ is $B$-linear. By construction $\varphi_V\eta^M_V=\eta^N_V f_V$ on every element of $M$. No finite presentation of $M$ is required; this argument checks all relations at once.

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tag 093S(3); elementary relations argument filling its omitted proof

proof.text: For every arrow $W\to V$, naturality restricts the equality of Step 4 to $\varphi_W\eta^M_W=\eta^N_W f_V$. Under the unit-compatible comparisons of Step 1, $\varphi|_V$ and the slice constant-sheaf map induced by $f_V$ therefore agree on every constant section over every object of $\mathcal C/V$. Each section of the source on the slice is locally such a constant section by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. Their images consequently agree on a covering, and separatedness of the target sheaf makes them equal. Thus the two sheaf morphisms agree. The cover $S$ of Step 2 works for every nondegenerate member, as required.

theorem exists_mem_forall_exists_constantSheafOverHom_comp_map_eq (M N : ModuleCat.{v'} Λ)
    [Module.Finite Λ M]
    (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{v'} Λ)).obj M ⟶ (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{v'} Λ)).obj N) :
    ∃ S ∈ J T, ∀ ⦃U : C⦄ (g : U ⟶ T), S g → (⊥ : Sieve U) ∉ J U → ∃ f : M ⟶ N,
      constantSheafOverHom J _ U M ≫ (J.overPullback _ U).map φ =
        (constantSheaf (J.over U) _).map f ≫ constantSheafOverHom J _ U N

Take T to be the arbitrary object U.
